view: Monday's +31.48% on 782.59M shares (4.8x the 60-day average) was an event repricing and short-squeeze-type reversal into heavy pre-existing fear. It was not a capitulation bar. The candle opened at 167.035, sold off to 156.93 and closed at 165.05, below its open and 3.8% under the 171.50 high, so supply showed up into strength, much of it from holders trapped between 162 and 171. Sentiment is no longer a contrarian tailwind at 165: the fear gauge that made the reaction so big has now been spent. Tactical: Wait, no chasing. Strategic: Hold the existing 30 shares. The ladder stays as approved, and any change needs the owner's approval.

Monday's bar: open 167.035, high 171.50, low 156.93, close 165.05. today_gap_open_pct is 33.1, and the close is below the open (a red body on a gap day). today_recovery_from_low_pct is 5.2, from a low that was itself 25.0% above Friday's close (today_low_vs_prev_close_pct). Reading: buyers paid up at the open, then sellers used the liquidity, and dip buyers absorbed at 156.93. That is event-driven re-rating with overhead supply, not a capitulation low. The capitulation-type signals were Friday's, and they have already resolved upward.

Volume was 782.59M, 4.8x the 60-day average and the highest of this sequence (Fri Nov 20 633.4M, Mon/Tue Nov 16/17 333.8M/406.9M in tv_chart_owner). Volume this large on a +31% day is a forced repositioning: short covering and de-hedging. Without options or short-interest data I cannot split covering from new longs, and covering-led rallies usually fade once the forced buying is done. Data conflict: structure.volume_spike_ratio_mon says 2.0, which contradicts 4.8. I use 4.8 because it matches 782.59M / 164.10M.

VIX is still elevated, so there is room for further relief if no new shock arrives, which supports the quarter view. But HY OAS widened on an up day, so credit did not join the relief. I weight that as a mild caution.

Owner bias audit, 'oversold = buy' and urgency: on 2026-11-22 oversold was real, and it paid only because a governance catalyst arrived. It is not oversold now. The urgency trap has flipped from 'buy before the bounce' to 'buy before it runs away'. The approved ladder answers that by design: C1 needs a fresh close at or below 145.71 then a close above it, and it never chases. There is no earnings binary until late Feb 2027. The near-dated binaries are the 2026-12-01/12-03 testimony window, the 10-Q (about 2026-12-04), FOMC 2026-12-09 and CPI 2026-12-10, and none of them justifies acting before its outcome is known.

notes_for_chair: Before-23-Nov question, signs that pointed to a sharp rebound (inputs/readings_2026-11-22.json). (1) Extreme, broad fear: VIX 35.90 (+26.28%), SOX -10.73%, S&P % above 200d at 45.92. (2) Retail already deeply bearish: AAII bearish 51.4, near the 1-year high of 53.3, but stale (Nov 11). CNN F&G 20 Extreme Fear, also stale (Nov 6). (3) Credit not stressed: HY OAS 3.52 (+0.05), so it was equity fear without a funding crisis. (4) Extreme oscillators on completed bars: weekly RSI14 25.01 (lowest since 2023, below the 35.7 at the Apr 2025 low), RSI7 11.78, weekly and daily stoch RSI 0/0, daily RSI14 15.05, 4H RSI7 7.84. (5) Climax-type volume: 633.4M on Nov 20 (3.9x), with 2.05B shares traded that week, the seventh straight down week and the worst since Oct 2008. (6) Price at a long-term anchor: 200W SMA 124.14 (1.1% above) and fib 0.5 at 127.09. (7) Outside view: after 2w drops of -15% or worse, n=4 gave 50/50/0 over 2w and 100/0/0 over 13w.

Before-23-Nov question, signs that did NOT point to a rebound. (1) Friday Nov 20 closed only 0.8% off its low, with no reversal bar. (2) Volume was accelerating through the week (333.8M, 406.9M, 633.4M), not drying up into a lower low. (3) Weekly MACD histogram -10.11 and BBPCT weekly -33.29 / daily -2.61 still falling, with no bullish divergence. (4) Price closed below the rising trendline from the 2023 lows (~140). (5) The Nov 12 high-volume reversal had already failed, so volume alone had a bad record. (6) The new SEC-accounting overhang was unresolved. (7) The governance read was that the board would NOT reinstate Huang (Chair Jones). No sentiment input could have timed Monday. The rebound came from a governance catalyst that the narrative evidence said was unlikely.

Lesson proposal for lessons-log (chair or owner to decide). Extreme fear and oversold readings did not time the low, but they set the size of the reaction. A +31.48% day is far outside NVDA's one-day history (one_day ge_+15 = 0.32%). My 2026-11-22 sentiment call was 2w 33/25/42 (down-skewed), resolving 2026-12-04, and price now sits far above its 131.81 up line. The volume description ('not capitulation') was accurate, but I gave too little weight to the asymmetry: with sentiment that washed out, a positive surprise moves price much more than a negative one. Next time, do not let a 'no reversal bar' read push 2w down far above base when fear is this broad.
